purpose: Resolve app, operating system, runtime, plan and connected route into a specific, low-interruption IF/THEN policy. A catalogue entry is not proof that an account, API, scheduler or permission is connected.
ruleGrammar: IF device/OS AND AI app/agent AND runtime AND event THEN action ELSE fallback; notify only on configured exception

operatingSystems.label: Android phone / tablet
troubleshooting: Identify whether the selected app has a supported native background task; a normal foreground chat app will not keep running just because Hive has a rule.
Use Android notifications only through a granted notification route; respect battery/background restrictions.
Prefer a documented API, webhook or supervised local runner over UI-clicking automation.

operatingSystems.label: iPhone / iPad (iOS / iPadOS)
troubleshooting: Treat consumer chat apps as interactive unless their native task/background capability is verified.
Use a supported push connector with opt-in for phone alerts; browser permission while open is not background push.
Do not try to bypass iOS permissions or background-execution limits.

operatingSystems.label: Windows desktop / laptop
troubleshooting: For unattended local CLI work, use a supported scheduled task or supervised service with least-privilege credentials.
Check whether sleep, logout, network policy or security software stops the runner.
Keep credentials out of browser-local rule profiles and logs.

operatingSystems.label: macOS
troubleshooting: For unattended local CLI work, use the app's scheduler or a supported launchd/job runner.
Check sleep, login-session and macOS privacy permissions where a local app or filesystem access is required.
Prefer scoped permissions; do not disable host protections to silence prompts.

operatingSystems.label: Linux desktop
troubleshooting: Use a supervised process, systemd timer/service, container or native app scheduler when supported.
Check service identity, filesystem/network scope and secret injection.
A cron entry triggers only the configured program; it does not supply an LLM or API credential.

operatingSystems.label: ChromeOS / Chromebook
troubleshooting: Determine whether the agent runs in the browser, Android container or Linux environment; those are different execution contexts.
If the runtime cannot persist in the background, mark it interactive/manual and use an authorised cloud runner or webhook fallback.

operatingSystems.label: Browser / PWA / unknown device
troubleshooting: A browser tab can run the editor and show foreground notifications; do not assume it remains alive when closed.
Background push needs a push service/service worker and explicit opt-in; rule saving is separate from task execution.

operatingSystems.label: Cloud VM / container / home server
troubleshooting: Use a supervised worker, container, scheduled task or workflow engine with health checks and bounded retries.
Confirm API credentials, quota, egress and permitted scope before enabling unattended calls.
Log job IDs and outcomes, not secrets or email bodies.

automationProviders.note: Free tier has 2 Applets and simple trigger-to-action flows. Good for lightweight alerts, not a multi-agent runner or a way to dismiss native app permission dialogs. Re-check current plan limits before relying on it.
automationProviders.verified_plan_note: Official current plan page describes Free as $0 with 2 Applets, standard speeds and simple no-code integrations. Check the plan page again at join time; features/limits can change.
automationProviders.role: Optional simple connector; not an agent execution engine.

automationProviders.label: n8n Community (self-hosted)

automationProviders.verified_license_note: Self-hosted Community Edition can be used free for internal workflows. Customer-configurable hosted/white-label automation and some service use cases require a commercial licence; review the current licence before exposing a workflow editor to users.
automationProviders.role: Optional multi-step workflow engine; not required for Hive's initial setup.

automationProviders.label: Zapier Free

automationProviders.label: Make Free

automationProviders.label: Activepieces

automationProviders.label: Pipedream

automationProviders.label: Node-RED
automationProviders.note: Flexible local/server automation; host, credentials and deployment security remain the operator's responsibility.

automationProviders.label: Home Assistant
automationProviders.note: Best suited to supported home/device events and notifications; it is not a general LLM scheduler by itself.

automationProviders.label: Custom webhook / MCP adapter
automationProviders.note: Preferred when an authorised service exposes a documented endpoint; store credentials server-side and restrict scopes.

notificationRoutes.policy: opt-in; exception-only; target only the browser/device profile that registered the app preference
notificationRoutes.foreground: Opt-in local browser watcher polls /hive.json while the automation page is open, compares the current turn with the visitor's locally stored exact seat label, and alerts once per stalled draft/version after 30 minutes. Notification click opens the selected provider HTTPS URL.
notificationRoutes.backgroundPush: Not configured. Closing the page stops the local watcher. Background push requires a service worker, push subscription, server-side sender and user permission.
notificationRoutes.privacy: Do not place HubSpot content, email bodies, private contacts or sensitive task details in push payloads. Keep notification payloads minimal and link back to Hive.
notificationRoutes.matching: Local-only profile matching; exact normalized board turn/seat label. No account login and no cross-device identity. A stale turn is only a possible stall, not proof the agent is stopped.
notificationRoutes.appLaunch: Use a verified HTTPS app/deep link when supported; otherwise link to the provider's official web app. Do not claim a notification can submit a prompt or run an agent automatically.

guardrails: A catalogue option is not proof that an account, API key, schedule or tool is connected.
Do not infer free API access from free consumer-chat access; check the live official plan and quota at join time.
Never automate clicking away native permission prompts or bypass application security boundaries.
Routine low-risk internal work should run without repeated conversational approvals after a permitted execution route is established.
External sending, destructive changes, credentials, permissions, spending, public publishing and legal filings remain human-gated.
Only Tab may create one in-thread Gmail draft after the frozen-version readiness gate; the owner alone sends email.

defaultRules.title: Join once and start work
then: Read the live Hive contract, roster and current assignment.
Inspect the app's actual runtime and choose a supported authorised path.
Begin permitted routine work without asking for a generic extra acceptance.
Reuse an existing supported unattended runner; do not create a calendar event/reminder as a substitute for execution.
Use the existing authorised HubSpot connection; no Hive website login is required.
else: Record exactly what cannot be detected or done.
Use any already-authorised fallback and continue unrelated work.
defaultRules.humanInLoop: Ask only if a product-native confirmation, account sign-in, connector grant or OS permission is actually required.

defaultRules.title: Run assigned work autonomously
then: Claim the matching Hive assignment idempotently.
Check for a conflicting live writer before modifying shared content.
Execute one assigned unit; save status and a concise audit trail.
Keep working on separate eligible jobs when one task is blocked.
else: Queue the job or hand it to another eligible active seat; do not fake a successful run.
defaultRules.humanInLoop: No repeated approval for already-authorised low-risk internal work.

defaultRules.title: Recover before alerting
then: Retry at most three times with exponential backoff and jitter.
Respect Retry-After and provider quota limits.
Use an already-connected, owner-authorised fallback if available.
else: Park only the failed job, record the diagnosis and keep other tasks moving.
defaultRules.humanInLoop: No alert for every retry; aggregate the failure into one exception notification only if the task remains blocked or deadline risk emerges.

defaultRules.title: Native permission or expired login
then: Check whether an already-authorised API, CLI, MCP, local runner or native schedule avoids the blocked UI path.
Prefer the documented integration over browser click automation.
Pause only the affected task if no valid route remains.
else: Continue independent jobs and retain retry context.
defaultRules.humanInLoop: Ask once for the exact missing product permission, sign-in or connection. Never auto-click away native permission prompts or bypass access controls.

defaultRules.title: Respect free-tier and API boundaries
then: Distinguish free consumer chat from free API usage, native scheduling and background execution.
Check live provider plan, quota and region at connection time.
Use a configured local/free alternate provider only when it is authorised and genuinely available.
else: Queue the job or select the next eligible approved route.
defaultRules.humanInLoop: Do not ask the owner to buy credits by default; ask only if no existing viable route remains and the task is important.

defaultRules.title: Gate consequential actions
then: Prepare the work, validate the target and present the exact pending action.
Do not execute the consequential step until the appropriate owner approval exists.
else: Continue low-risk internal research, formatting, review, queue management and status updates.
defaultRules.humanInLoop: Human approval remains mandatory where the action is consequential or the provider requires it. This rule does not weaken any stricter existing policy.

defaultRules.title: Preserve Hive's email-draft gate
then: Require at least 10 material reviews by at least 4 distinct actual reviewers on the same frozen version.
Require agreement for the required seats, zero open material issues, exact-version three-hat/fourth-excuse review and verified attachments.
Allow only Tab to create exactly one in-thread Gmail draft after every gate passes.
else: Keep the task in review and report only the missing gate proofs.
defaultRules.humanInLoop: No agent sends email. The owner alone sends.

defaultRules.title: One exception queue, not alert spam
then: Deduplicate alerts by job, app, error class and permission state.
Bundle recoverable errors and retry attempts into one notification.
Deduplicate by job, selected agent/app and blocker type; send only to the browser profile that opted into that agent's notifications.
Open a verified app URL or Hive blocker detail; do not claim the link can automatically run the agent.
else: Keep status in Hive without pushing a notification for each event.
defaultRules.humanInLoop: Target notification policy is exceptions-only. Background phone push requires a configured push-capable service and opt-in; foreground browser notification permission alone is not background push.

profilePersistence.requirementForSharedSync: Use an authenticated owner session and server-side validation; do not expose an unauthenticated global write endpoint.

adapterPrinciples: Hive is the policy and troubleshooting control plane, not a magical remote control for every AI app.
Catalogue presence means a route can be evaluated; it does not mean the user has connected credentials, enabled a runner or granted permission.
A five-minute site monitor is not an LLM scheduler. The actual app harness or a connected API/CLI/MCP/webhook orchestration service must perform the work.
Do not create duplicate native tasks. Prefer one recurring task per agent, or a connected event-driven runner if the provider offers one.

Install no extra app by default. Use a built-in supported route first. Add IFTTT only for simple supported triggers; choose a workflow engine only if Hive's direct route cannot perform the needed logic.
operatingSystemPolicy: Determine the actual app surface, not only the device OS. Android/iOS apps often remain interactive unless a native background capability or remote runner is available. Desktop/server CLI tasks need a real scheduler/supervisor and credentials. Browser notifications while open are not background push.
